direct_answer: Splints can support painful hand or thumb joints, particularly the base of the thumb. Some people wear them at night or during tasks. A hand therapist or occupational therapist can advise and fit them. Check skin and report swelling or numbness.

content:
Hand osteoarthritis can make daily grip painful.

This guide covers splints. It is educational information, not a diagnosis or personal treatment plan.

How splints help

Splints support a joint and may ease pain during rest or tasks.

Getting the right fit

  • Ask your GP for referral to hand therapy.
  • Off-the-shelf splints may help but fit matters.

Skin checks

  • Check for red marks.
  • Remove if fingers become numb, cold or swollen.

Medicines, reviews and hand OA

Topical anti-inflammatories may help hand OA. Ask a pharmacist before using.

When to get help

  • Call 999 for chest pain, trouble breathing, signs of a stroke, or a fall with a possible serious injury.
  • Get urgent advice the same day (NHS 111 or your GP) for sudden confusion, a sudden drop in mobility, or a hot, swollen joint with fever.
  • See your GP for a steady decline over weeks, unplanned weight loss or repeated falls.

Never stop or change a prescribed medicine yourself. Ask your GP or pharmacist for a review.

Common questions

Should I wear it all day?

Follow advice; usually not all the time.

Will it stop OA?

No, it helps symptoms.

Sources and further reading

  • NHS: Osteoarthritis
  • NHS: Osteoarthritis treatment
